newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen stuck in limited range.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen stuck in limited range.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to be stuck in a limited range on Friday amid caution ahead of the Group of Seven (G7) summit meeting this weekend, brokers said.

They said the yen's slight decline against the dollar and firmness in Nikkei futures in Chicago overnight would support the market but a newspaper report concerning Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd could hurt shares in the brokerage sector.
On Thursday, the Nikkei 225 average ended up 10 points, or 0.05 percent, at 20,507.85. Its September futures slipped 140 points to finish the day at 20,440.
"People are unwilling to move much ahead of Denver summit," said a trader at a foreign securities house.
Brokers said the market was cautious about currencies, which may be affected by the outcome of the summit.
The dollar stood around 114.60 yen in early Asia trade on Friday, up from 113.40/50 yen in late Tokyo on Thursday.
In Chicago, the Nikkei average's September futures closed at 20,605, up from their close of 20,440 in Osaka on Thursday.
